svg.text: Round 2's ldmatrix copies, line by line
Shared memory → registers for the four operands of the two multiplies: Q and K for S = Q Kᵀ, P and V for O = P·V.
Q, K and V tiles are 64 × 64 bf16; 4 warps, each owning 16 rows of the block's 64. A step k is 16 head dims of S's sum (or 16 keys of O's).

svg.text: Q, one step k: 64 rows × 16 head dims
make_tiled_copy_A copies the tiled MMA's A operand layout, so the copy hands each
lane exactly the values its multiply reads. No thread layout is written by hand.
With (4, 1, 1), each warp multiplies only its own 16 rows, so on step k it loads
only those: 16 rows × 16 head dims, four 8 × 8 tiles, one ldmatrix.x4.
P is the A operand of O = P·V, so the same copy loads it too.
The same for the B operand: K

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: K, one step k: 64 keys × 16 head dims
make_tiled_copy_B does the same for the B operand. Each warp computes all 64 keys of
its rows, so every warp needs the whole step: 64 keys × 16 head dims, four 16 × 16
Pieces are 16 keys wide because of permutation_mnk = (64, 16, 16). With the default
8 keys, each instruction would carry only two tiles, and K would need twice as many
B again, for O = P·V: V, transposed on the way

text.font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace
ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace

svg.text: One 8 × 8 tile of V as stored. Orange:
In shared memory V is stored like K: one key per row, head dims along the row.
The multiply wants each lane's 2 values to lie along the dimension it sums over. For
S = Q Kᵀ that is head dims, along a stored row: the plain load. For O = P·V it is
transpose=True (ldmatrix.trans) swaps each tile's rows and columns as it loads, so V
needs no separate transpose. Otherwise the copy is the same as K's: 4 ldmatrix.x4
Run it: copy step k of Q from shared memory into registers

svg.text: None keeps a whole mode: all of the thread's values and row
pieces. k picks step k: head dims 16k to 16k + 15, for k = 0
Each warp issues one ldmatrix.x4 for its 16 rows. The K, P and V copies are the same
line with their own copy and tensors.
Per key block, each warp issues 40 ldmatrix: Q 4 × 1 + K 4 × 4 + P 4 × 1 + V 4 × 4. Rounds 0–1 used 224 plain loads (LDS) for the same values.
